alex: Heads up — found a discrepancy between the Python and TS SDKs for array params on /v1/completions. Python ends up sending keys with explicit null, TS omits them. Server behavior diverges. Can we decide a standard? :eyes:
meera: Which param(s) are we talking about? stop tokens or something else like logit_bias / user_metadata? examples pls.
sam: if it's stop that could be bad, different behavior is subtle and easy to ship.
alex: repro is stop and an optional array field called `user_metadata`. Minimal difference: Python client serializes `stop: null` when user passes None, TS client drops the key entirely. Server treats `null` as an explicit empty array for stop which changes early stopping.
meera: can you paste the payloads and the server responses?

alex: ```
# Python-sent JSON (body)
{
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "prompt": "hi",
  "stop": null,
  "user_metadata": null
}

# TS-sent JSON (body)
{
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "prompt": "hi"
}
```

alex: Server: when `stop` present and null => server treats as [] and stops immediately on match; when absent => uses model default (no forced stop). Responses differ (tokens truncated).

jess: Yikes. We should decide: absence == use default; explicit null should not change semantics unless we want it to. My vote: server should treat explicit null for optional arrays as equivalent to missing (i.e., ignore).

meera: I agree for arrays/lists used as optional params. But we should be conservative: for objects/maps (e.g., logit_bias) null might mean explicit reset. Need clear rule: "for optional list params, null -> missing". Document it.

sam: Implementation plan: 1) server accepts null->treat as missing for list-type params; 2) py-sdk stop sending `"stop": null` by default (drop None). That keeps TS behavior. 3) add backwards-compat tests.

alex: @meera can you own the py-sdk change? It's a small serializer tweak: omit keys where value is None for optional arrays. I'll open a tiny server PR to normalize null arrays to missing at parse time.

meera: I can take the SDK change. Suggest adding a flag like `explicit_null:true` if user really wants to send null for some reason (rare). I'll draft a short design note and a unit test.

jess: I've filed an issue with payloads + failing test: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/4321 — tag: regression/stop-behavior. Added example curl and expected vs actual outputs. :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout 2% applied to inference-service/stable at 2026-03-17T14:35Z

alex: Thanks. After the server patch lands I'll run the langhooks regression suite and then we can bump canary to 10% for extra smoke. Ping infra for a quick perf check (batching/kv cache unaffected).

meera: I'll open the SDK PR tonight and add serialization tests. Will tag you all in the PR for review.

alex: Great — ping me for review, I'll add a tiny e2e that posts both payload styles and asserts identical model behavior.

sam: Also add a changelog note in the server repo under "internal behavior normalizations" so we have a record.

jess: noted. Thanks team.
